Design Criterion A

Inquiring and Analyzing

Justification of Need

Rawalpindi faces significant urbanization and infrastructure challenges. The Faizabad interchange is a critical nexus attracting daily wage laborers and migrants who often find themselves without safe shelter. Exposed to extreme weather—from 45°C summers to freezing winters—the need for a flexible, accessible, and dignified shelter is paramount for immediate public health and safety.

Research & Analysis

Primary Research

  • • Needs Assessment Surveys
  • • Stakeholder Interviews (NGOs)
  • • Site Analysis (Faizabad)

Secondary Research

  • • Poverty Statistics Analysis
  • • Climatic Data Review
  • • Existing Shelter Models

Existing Product Gaps

Panahgahs

Overcrowded, limited privacy.

Emergency Tents

Poor insulation, low durability.

Container Homes

High cost, thermal issues.

Problem Statement

"Vulnerable populations lack safe, climate-resilient shelter with integrated utilities. Our goal: Modular urban micro-shelters fostering dignity."

Design Criterion B

Developing Ideas

Chosen Design: Flexi-Pod

The Modular Panel Shelter was chosen for its optimal balance of durability, rapid deployment, and thermal performance.

4-6 m²

Personal Space

150W

Solar Power

0.5m

Elevated Base

EPS

Insulated Core

⚡ Electricity

12V system, 100Ah battery, 2 LED lights, USB ports for communication.

🔥 Cooking/Gas

Ventilated compartment for 5kg LPG cylinder with safety CO detectors.

🚽 Sanitation

Urine-diverting composting toilet with solar ventilation fans.

🏗️ Structure

Galvanized steel frame with 50mm insulated sandwich panels.

Design Criterion C

Creating the Solution

Logical Creation Plan

Weeks 1-3: Procurement

Material sourcing and logistics planning.

Week 4: Site Prep

Foundations and infrastructure trenching.

Weeks 5-8: Assembly

Modular panel erection and utility rough-ins.

Weeks 9-10: Handover

Final QC, finishing, and occupant orientation.

Assembly Workflow

01

Secure base frame on foundation plinths.

02

Install wall and roof sandwich panels.

03

Integrate solar panels and electrical wiring.

04

Plumbing installation (sinks & composting toilet).

05

Fit out interior: desk, shelving, and folding cot.

Design Criterion D

Evaluating Success

Testing Methods

Structural & Resilience

Simulated wind load and rainfall testing; thermal monitoring of interior temperatures vs. Rawalpindi's ambient peaks.

Utility Validation

Voltage/ampere verification for solar, leak detection for water systems, and composting effectiveness audits.

Impact on Occupants

Improved health, hygiene, safety, and dignity. Fosters economic stability by providing a secure base near transit hubs.

Impact on Rawalpindi

Reduced social burden, improved urban aesthetics, and a replicable model for sustainable migrant support.

Future Iterations
